title: When the Bridge Burns
premise: In the river city of Vellum's Reach, on the eve of the Printers' Revolt, Ivo Okafor works her late father's type cases in a shop that serves both the governor's press and the underground pamphleteers. When the seasonal bridge closes, the city is sealed, and Ivo discovers her father secretly cut the plates that forged the governor's fraudulent land grants — the inheritance that made her family complicit. To redeem it, she must print the true ledger and smuggle it out before the victors' historians rewrite the record, knowing the truth will burn her family's name along with the governor's. She succeeds at terrible cost: the bridge burns in the revolt's final night, the ledger survives, and Ivo chooses to sign her father's name beside her own on the last page.
about_author: Y. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print shops across West Africa and the Caribbean. Their novels examine what ordinary craftspeople carry when history turns violent.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. As the bridge closes for the season, Ivo finishes a rush order for the governor's office and notices the type doesn't match her father's hand — someone has been using his matrices. The emotional beat is quiet unease: her careful invisibility begins to feel like complicity as the first pamphlets appear on the shop doorstep.

chapters.title: What the Matrices Keep
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with a flashback in her father's voice via his workshop journal. She discovers the forged land-grant plates hidden in the type case's false bottom and realizes her father cut them under coercion — and that the underground wants them as evidence. Rising tension: the governor's men begin searching print shops, and Ivo must decide whether to hide the plates or use them.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, intercut with an apprentice's testimony. The revolt ignites; the governor's soldiers raid the shop, and Ivo prints the true ledger in the chaos, hiding pages in paper bales bound for the bridge. Climax: she is caught between the raiders and the mob, and the bridge is set alight with her only copy of the ledger aboard.

chapters.title: The Record
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, months later in the provisional archive. The ledger pages, scorched but legible, were pulled from the river by the apprentice she once protected. Facing the victors' historians who want a cleaner story, Ivo testifies, signing both her father's name and her own. The resolution is bittersweet: truth preserved, inheritance redeemed but never whole.
